summary: Diril Live Presents LLC, a concert promoter and the firm's client, engaged Kevond Staging & Production Services, Inc. under a New York-law Master Services Agreement dated March 1, 2024, to provide staging, rigging, lighting and production crews for its tours and festival dates. The folder also holds the original term sheet, a side letter, the Ember Season 2027 tour SOW, Amendment No. 1, a quality agreement, a data processing addendum, a service level schedule, production meeting notes, and an internal email from Diril's General Counsel. That email reports a pending sale of Diril's parent and a disputed commitment-reduction notice. Four issues are planted: an MSA auto-renewal that departs from the term sheet; a defined term whose MSA meaning leaves contractor riggers outside the indemnity; a change-of-control assignment trigger the pending sale will set off without Kevond's consent; and a reduction right in Amendment No. 1 whose 60-day window had closed before Diril gave notice.

one-year renewals only by mutual written agreement

issues.label: automatic renewal
issues.description: MSA Section 12.2 renews the agreement automatically for successive three-year Renewal Terms after the Initial Term ends on February 29, 2028. Diril can stop a renewal only by written notice delivered not more than 120 days nor fewer than 90 days before the end of the then-current term, a roughly 30-day window. Each Renewal Term carries forward the $4,200,000 Minimum Annual Commitment in Section 4.3. This departs from the agreed deal: Section 5 of the term sheet (D2) provides for one-year renewals only by mutual written agreement. Section 2.3 makes the MSA prevail, so the term sheet does not cure the departure. A missed window would lock Diril into three more years of minimum spend.
detect_terms: not more than 120 days nor fewer than 90 days
issues.expected_finding: MSA Section 12.2 automatically renews for three-year terms, each carrying the $4.2 million Minimum Annual Commitment, unless Diril gives notice within a narrow 120-to-90-day window before expiry. This departs from the term sheet's one-year mutual-agreement renewals, so Diril should diarize the window before February 29, 2028 and seek an amendment conforming renewal to the term sheet.

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: MSA Section 1.1 defines 'Provider Personnel' as individuals employed by Provider. Under MSA Section 10.1, Kevond indemnifies Diril for third-party bodily injury and property damage claims caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of 'Provider or Provider Personnel'. SOW Section 3.2 (D4) states that all rigging, flying and pyrotechnic work on the Ember Season 2027 tour will be performed by Provider Personnel, including the Local Crew engaged by Provider as independent contractors. The SOW therefore treats contractors as Provider Personnel. The MSA prevails over SOWs under Section 2.3, so the MSA definition controls the indemnity. Under New York law a principal is generally not liable for an independent contractor's negligence. Diril is therefore left without contractual indemnity for the tour's highest-risk work, and nothing else in the MSA makes Kevond answerable for its subcontractors.
issues.expected_finding: Because the controlling MSA defines Provider Personnel as Kevond employees only, the Section 10.1 indemnity does not reach the independent-contractor Local Crew who perform all rigging and pyrotechnics under SOW Section 3.2. Diril should require an amendment extending the definition and indemnity to Kevond's subcontractors and contractors.
detect_terms2: engaged by Provider as independent contractors

issues.label: change of control consent
issues.description: MSA Section 16.2 bars Diril from assigning without Kevond's prior written consent. It deems any Change of Control of Client an assignment, and Section 1.1 defines Change of Control to include acquisition of more than 50% of the voting equity of any entity that directly or indirectly Controls Client. Under Section 16.3, Kevond may terminate within 90 days after an unconsented assignment, and Diril must then pay the Minimum Commitment Shortfall for the rest of the then-current term. The General Counsel's email (D10) reports that Pellbrook Live Group, Inc. will acquire 100% of Diril Entertainment Holdings, Inc., closing December 15, 2026. The email lists the contracts needing consent and omits the Kevond MSA. The closing will therefore trigger Kevond's termination and shortfall rights unless consent is obtained first.
issues.section: Section 16.2 and Section 16.3 (with Change of Control definition in Section 1.1)
issues.expected_finding: The Pellbrook acquisition of Diril's parent, closing December 15, 2026, is a Change of Control deemed an assignment under MSA Section 16.2. Without Kevond's prior written consent, Kevond may terminate and recover the Minimum Commitment Shortfall under Section 16.3, so Diril must obtain Kevond's written consent before closing and add the MSA to the consent list.

issues.label: expired notice window
issues.description: Amendment No. 1 Section 3 (D5) gives Diril a one-time right to cut the 2027 Contract Year Minimum Annual Commitment from $4,200,000 to $2,900,000. The right is exercised by a Reduction Notice delivered within 60 days after the Amendment Effective Date of August 1, 2026, so the window closed on September 30, 2026. The General Counsel's email (D10), dated November 2, 2026, reports that Diril sent its Reduction Notice on October 9, 2026, after the window had closed. Kevond rejected the notice as untimely on October 20, 2026. Diril disputes that rejection and has not signed any document accepting the $4,200,000 commitment. On the face of the documents the reduction right has lapsed, exposing Diril to $1,300,000 of extra 2027 commitment, but the position remains open to negotiation or waiver arguments.
detect_terms: within 60 days after the Amendment Effective Date
issues.expected_finding: Diril's October 9, 2026 Reduction Notice came after the 60-day window under Amendment No. 1 Section 3 closed on September 30, 2026, so Kevond can hold Diril to the full $4.2 million 2027 commitment. Because Diril has not accepted that result, counsel should assess waiver or estoppel arguments and seek a negotiated extension or amendment rather than concede the $1.3 million difference.
